item.title: Kennedy Center board votes to restore Trump's name on building
item.description: The Kennedy Center's board of trustees voted to add President Trump's name to the facade of the performing arts center, more than two months after a judge ordered its removal, according to a Democrat who sits on the center's board.

item.title: Mostly-Trump-appointed board votes to restore his name on the Kennedy Center
item.description: President Trump's name may once again appear on the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. It came down this summer after a federal judge said only Congress could order a name change, but the president's allies apparently have a new plan. Ed O'Keefe reports.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's private texts, internet searches, notes read aloud in court
item.description: Lindsay Clancy appeared more composed in court on Thursday as the jury heard about her internet searches and private text messages. Shanelle Kaul has more details.

item.title: NTSB reveals why a Ryanair window may have smashed open mid-flight
item.description: Last month, a Ryanair window smashed open mid-flight, causing a passenger's head to be pulled through the opening before other passengers yanked him back in. Kris Van Cleave has new details about why this happened.

item.title: David Crowley begins campaign as Democratic nominee for governor in Wisconsin
item.description: Democrat David Crowley has kicked off his general election campaign for Wisconsin governor after his win over Francesca Hong in Tuesday's primary. Republican strategist Doug Heye and Ofirah Yheskel, director of external affairs for the Democratic Governors Association, join "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Luigi Mangione may be preparing to take plea deal, sources say
item.description: Luigi Mangione, the man accused of killing UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, may be preparing to accept a plea agreement, avoiding a federal trial and possibly life in prison, sources say. Tom Hanson reports.

item.title: Dozens need rescuing in Indiana as streets turn to rivers amid flooding emergency
item.description: Another round of dangerous storms brought heavy rain over part of the U.S., already beyond its limits. The Midwest was hit again with the worst of it, with the brunt falling on Indiana on Thursday. Ian Lee reports and Lonnie Quinn has the forecast.

item.title: Tropical storm forms near Hawaii, hurricane watch issued for the Big Island
item.description: Tropical Storm Lala could bring rain, high winds and dangerous surf and rip currents to the Hawaiian Islands this weekend.

item.title: Trump in legal battle with Capital One after accounts closed over money laundering concerns in 2021
item.description: Capital One says it closed some of President Trump and his organization's accounts in 2021 because of money laundering concerns. Trump has sued the bank over the closures, alleging political retaliation following the Jan. 6 Capitol riot. Ross Delston, attorney and anti-money laundering expert, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Details on potential Luigi Mangione plea deal
item.description: Luigi Mangione, who is accused in the 2024 killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, is in discussions about a possible plea deal on federal charges in the case, sources tell CBS News. CBS News legal contributor Caroline Polisi has more.

item.title: Democratic senators demand answers about conditions aboard USS Abraham Lincoln
item.description: Senate Democrats are demanding answers about conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln during the aircraft carrier's record-setting deployment.

item.title: Latest from the White House on Strait of Hormuz, Trump's secret plane switch
item.description: CBS News' Ed O'Keefe reports from the White House on claims from both the U.S. and Iran about control of the Strait of Hormuz and the latest details on President Trump's secret plane switch in Turkey.

item.title: U.S. and Iran both claim control of Strait of Hormuz as questions grow about conflict's expansion
item.description: Matthew Kroenig served in the Department of Defense and the intelligence community in three presidential administrations, including President Trump's first term. He joins "The Takeout" to discuss the latest news on the Iran war.

item.title: Flock CEO responds to abuses of its surveillance technology
item.description: The CEO of Flock Safety apologized for alleged abuses of its service by law enforcement officers as the company rolled out new changes to how it operates.

item.title: What to know about USS Lincoln as concerns raised about 9-month deployment, conditions on board
item.description: Senate Democrats are demanding answers about the conditions crew members are facing on the USS Abraham Lincoln. The ship has been deployed since Nov, 21, 2025, and its deployment has been repeatedly extended. CBS News' Major Garrett and Charlie D'Agata have the latest.

item.title: Luigi Mangione in discussions about possible guilty plea, sources say
item.description: Luigi Mangione, accused in the 2024 killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, is in discussions about a possible plea deal on federal charges, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: CEO Tim Cook touts Apple's push for American manufacturing, discusses his legacy
item.description: CBS News' Jo Ling Kent speaks with outgoing CEO Tim Cook about Apple's new focus on American manufacturing and what he thinks he's stood for as the head of the company.

item.title: University of Michigan plans to forgo letter grades for some first-semester freshmen next year
item.description: The University of Michigan plans to forgo letter grades for some first-semester freshmen next year, prompting debate over the usefulness and impact of grades. Abbie Everett, senior director of teaching and learning at KnowledgeWorks, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: State Police investigators testify about search history in Lindsay Clancy trial
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's trial for the murders of her three children in Massachusetts resumed Thursday with testimony from State Police investigators.

item.title: AI is driving up consumer prices. That won't stop anytime soon.
item.description: Surging AI investment is pushing up the cost of smartphones and other gadgets, according to analysts. Here's why.

item.title: Jury selected for Tupac Shakur murder trial, opening statements expected Monday
item.description: A jury of six men and 10 women was selected to hear the case against an ex-gang leader accused of orchestrating Tupac Shakur's killing​ nearly 30 years ago.

item.title: Luigi Mangione discussing possible plea deal in federal case, sources say
item.description: Luigi Mangione, the man accused of murdering United Healthcare CEO Brian Thompson, is in discussions about a possible plea deal in his federal case, sources say. CBS News' legal contributor Jessica Levinson has more.

item.title: Becky G gives Gayle King an exclusive behind-the-scenes look at rehearsal
item.description: "CBS Mornings" co-host Gayle King went inside a rehearsal with singer Becky G as she gives fans a sneak peek at a new single before her upcoming album's release.

item.title: Record-breaking heat takes mounting toll on the U.S. economy
item.description: Heat waves are dealing a financial blow to businesses and creating hazardous conditions for workers, according to climate experts.

item.title: Trump's secret plane switch took place within a day of credible missile threat
item.description: President Trump secretly moved from Air Force One to another plane within a day of U.S. and Turkish intelligence picking up on an Iranian plot to fire a missile at the jet, CBS News has learned.

item.title: Trump administration's antisemitism lawsuit against Harvard dismissed
item.description: The lawsuit was one of many steps against Harvard that the Trump administration has taken since President Trump's return to office, in addition to attempting to cancel billions of dollars in federal funds.

item.title: Becky G reflects on advocacy in new music, rise to fame
item.description: Becky G spoke exclusively with "CBS Mornings" co-host Gayle King about her rise to fame, being the breadwinner of the family at a young age and her new music.

item.title: Watch: Total solar eclipse mesmerizes crowds throughout Europe
item.description: On August 12, 2026, a total solar eclipse awed onlookers throughout Europe, including in Spain and the United Kingdom.

item.title: Stunning photos show total solar eclipse over Europe
item.description: The only total solar eclipse of 2026 crossed the Northern Hemisphere Wednesday, with a path of totality across parts of Greenland, Iceland and northern Spain. See photos and video from the best viewing locations.

item.title: Do you have a tip for 60 Minutes? Here's how to send it to us
item.description: For 57 years, 60 Minutes has been asking tough questions and telling powerful stories. Often, it starts with information sent in by viewers. Here's how to send yours to our journalists confidentially.
